title: Your first request
task: Send a real request with curl and look at the raw response, headers first.

checks.prompt: Does the output start with a status line like HTTP/2 200 before any HTML?
Can you find a Content-Type header in the output?

hints.text: -i stands for include: it prints the response headers above the body.
Everything above the first blank line is metadata; below it is the body.

title: Send query parameters
task: Echo your own query parameters back using httpbin and see how the server parsed them.

checks.prompt: In the JSON response, does the args object show course and lesson as separate keys?

hints.text: Quote the whole URL so the shell does not eat the &.
Look at the args key in the response body.

title: Echo a POST and a PUT
task: Send a POST and a PUT with a JSON body to httpbin and inspect what arrived.

checks.prompt: Does the json field in the response show the name key you sent?
Does the response show the request went to /post the first time and /put the second?

hints.text: -X chooses the method, -H adds a header, -d sets the body.
The response echoes the request; find your payload under json or data.

title: Collect status codes
task: Provoke a 200, a 404, and a 401 from real endpoints and read only the status lines.

checks.prompt: Did you get 200, 404, and 401 in that order?
Can you say why the last one was 401 and not 403?

hints.text: -o /dev/null discards the body; -w prints a custom string afterwards.
The last endpoint needs credentials you did not send: that is 401, not 403.

title: Negotiate a content type
task: Ask the same endpoint for two different formats with the Accept header.

checks.prompt: Does the first call wrap the message in a JSON object and the second return plain text?

hints.text: Accept tells the server what you want back; the server decides.

title: Pull one field from JSON
task: Fetch repository metadata and extract a single nested field with python3.
commands: curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/michael-borck/cairn | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['owner']['login'], d['license']['spdx_id'])"

checks.prompt: Does the second command print the owner login and the licence SPDX id instead of the whole document?

hints.text: Owner is itself an object; drill down with two keys in a row.

solution: curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/michael-borck/cairn | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['owner']['login'], d['license']['spdx_id'])"

title: Send a bearer token
task: See the difference between calling a protected endpoint with no token and with a token in the Authorization header.

checks.prompt: Without the header, does the endpoint answer 401?
With the header, does the JSON response show authenticated: true (it does not validate the token, just its presence)?

hints.text: Credentials travel in a header, never in the URL.
The scheme comes first: Authorization: Bearer <token>.

title: Read the whole exchange
task: Use curl -v to watch the full conversation, including the redirect hop.

checks.prompt: Do you see more than one request: a 302 with a Location header, then the final 200?
Does > mark lines your client sent and < mark lines the server returned?

hints.text: -v prints the conversation to stderr; pipe stderr into the pager too.
Count the status lines: one per hop.
